text:
Alex Kim: FYI during tonight's oncall we had two folks try to operate on the same tenant replay at once. Ended up coordinating in #eng-sre which is messy. We should add a tiny operator-claim primitive to the replay UI/API so someone can take ownership and leave a short note.

Priya Desai: Strong +1. Prefer a lightweight coordination token rather than changing compute or quotas. Something ephemeral, TTL-backed.

Omar Chen: We already have leasing.service used elsewhere. Could POST /v1/replays/:id/claims that returns a claim_token and expiry. Store token in replay metadata for visibility.

Lina Ortiz: UI idea: show "Claim" CTA beside the replay header. If claimed show owner avatar, contact, TTL countdown, and small "Extend" / "Release" controls. Also let users add a short note (what they're doing).

Alex Kim: Gate list: destructive control-plane actions (cancel, rerun, change-priority) should require the claim token. Reads (logs, status) remain free. That prevents accidental interference.

Priya Desai: Agreed. Implementation should avoid large migrations. Add nullable columns and no heavy backfill.

Omar Chen: Proposed metadata columns (nullable): claim_token VARCHAR, claimed_by VARCHAR, claim_expires_at TIMESTAMP, claim_note TEXT. Keep default NULL for old rows.

Lina Ortiz: UX behaviour: explicit "Extend" button. Also the console may emit a small heartbeat while the detail pane is open so TTL doesn't drift while active. But do not auto-extend silently.

Alex Kim: Security: start scope to Platform + SRE roles. Later make it org-configurable. Audit all claim ops to audit log.

ops-bot: Feature flag note: replay.claims_ui default OFF. Toggle via FF service for canary teams.

Priya Desai: Tests: unit tests for lease collisions, integration that rejects cancel/rerun without claim_token, e2e for claim/extend/release flow on console.

Omar Chen: Draft API sketch:

POST /v1/replays/{replay_id}/claims
Request body: { "owner": "alex.kim", "contact": "pager:alex", "note": "investigating missing hours" }
Response: { "claim_token": "ct_abc123", "expires_at": "2026-04-01T03:20:00Z", "owner": "alex.kim" }

POST /v1/replays/{replay_id}/claims/extend  (body: { "claim_token": "ct_abc123" })
DELETE /v1/replays/{replay_id}/claims  (header: X-Claim-Token: ct_abc123)

Server validates claim_token via leasing.service before allowing gated actions. TTL default 30m.

Lina Ortiz: Console flow: if operator attempts a gated action without a claim, show modal: "Action requires an active claim. Claim now and proceed?" Provide quick one-click claim option that sets a short note.

Alex Kim: Observability: emit telemetry.operator_claim_seconds and gauge telemetry.active_claims_count. Dashboard tile: "Active claimed replays" with avg hold time and quick links.

Priya Desai: Also log claim lifecycle events to existing replay audit trail so history shows who held it and for how long.

Omar Chen: Migration plan: add nullable columns mentioned earlier, no backfill. Replayer service picks up claim info and broadcasts via existing websocket update channel.

ops-bot: Ticket created: PLT-3281 "Operator claim token for replay coordination"  Assignees: Alex Kim, Omar Chen, Lina Ortiz. Feature flag replay.claims_ui OFF by default.

Alex Kim: I'll open the RFC + PR for server side bits. Lina, please attach a quick mock for the Claim button and modal. Priya, can you own tests?

Priya Desai: Got it. I'll draft integration tests and a small e2e.

Lina Ortiz: Mock landing shortly. Thinking small: claim badge, TTL hover, extend/release inline.

Alex Kim: Nice. Let's keep this minimal: coordination only, no quota or compute semantics. After canary we'll iterate.

ops-bot: Locking thread as work moves to PLT-3281. :white_check_mark:
